newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch flower auction passes 2.5bn guilder level.
newsitem.headline: Dutch flower auction passes 2.5bn guilder level.

text.p: Bloemenveiling Aalsmeer, the world's largest flower auction, said it expects a record turnover for 1996 of 2.54 billion guilders with net profit 30 percent up on 1995's 40 million guilders.

In a statement, the flower auction added transactions early on Thursday sent turnover for this year past the 2.5 billion guilder level. In 1995, turnover at 2.4 billion guilders was three percent down on the previous year's record.
Sales of cut plants and flowers to Germany, France and Britain have been especially strong this year, it said.
Dutch tulips have been far and away the most popular flower with overseas importers and the auction said it has a 50 percent share in the world tulip market.

However the auction's managers noted that its market split is changing. While imports of Dutch flowers are growing in Europe, new international competition is keeping its ambitions to develop in new, far-flung countries, under pressure. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
